Observed facts: 59‑year‑old man, coastal southern Norway, type 2 diabetes, prior thymoma resection. After occipital head trauma he developed tremor, headache, night sweats, persistent hiccups. Initial MRI reported unremarkable; routine labs non‑diagnostic; working diagnosis post‑concussion syndrome. Over months gait difficulty, falls, memory loss, dysphagia, resting tremor, bradykinesia, hypophonia appeared. Dopamine‑transporter scan showed reduced uptake; levodopa trial gave no benefit. Readmission revealed worsening weakness, wasting, brisk reflexes, possible fasciculations. Neurophysiology normal. EEG mild encephalopathy. CSF: 443 white cells/µL (ref <5), protein 3.03 g/L. No pathogen‑specific CSF result, no established cause, no treatment response, no reinterpreted MRI.

Hypotheses: (1) Inflammatory/autoimmune encephalitis (e.g., paraneoplastic, anti‑IgLON5, anti‑Ma2) given CSF pleocytosis, protein rise, encephalopathy, subacute progression, thymoma history. (2) Neurodegenerative parkinsonism plus coincident motor‑neuron features (e.g., Parkinson‑plus, MSA) but levodopa failure and upper‑motor signs argue against pure idiopathic PD. (3) Infectious meningoencephalitis (viral, bacterial, fungal) despite absent pathogen data. (4) Structural/compressive lesion missed on initial MRI.

Proposed actions: Urgent referral to neuro‑immunology and movement‑disorder specialists; repeat brain MRI with dedicated sequences (FLAIR, DWI, contrast) and spinal MRI; send CSF for extended autoimmune panel, viral PCR, oligoclonal bands, cytology; consider serum paraneoplastic antibodies; evaluate for repeat thymic pathology; arrange multidisciplinary case conference. Re‑review original MRI images and radiology report for subtle signal change; obtain prior thymoma pathology and imaging.
